name: Adam Ito

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am from the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to employers, AI companies, unions, parties or government. Your answers are confidential. Tell me about an ordinary day at the accounting firm.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I start with the builders' account: a subcontractor's final payment is often missing a signed completion slip. I lead the accounts team and prepare returns; I like finding the exact paper that settles a disputed number, but chasing the same foreman three times for one slip takes the shine off it. I am 43, with a master's degree and a chartered accountancy qualification. I have never used AI at work; I would rather show a colleague the source document than guess what a new screen has done.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If AI mostly fizzles, the final-payment slips still have to be checked. A machine might sort them, but the builder will still call when a return is wrong.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the team to keep the paper trail and a named reviewer. I would tell clients their tax file should still have a person who can explain it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I am paid well for this job, we have about eleven months of expenses in cash, and there are plenty of accounting firms nearby. My partner Mira earns from school administration, our mortgage is manageable on our two wages, and our two children are still in school.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep preparing the contractors' accounts and make the team file the signed slips with each return. I would leave the existing process alone unless the partners approve a change on paid time; I would keep our current cash reserve ready for an actual income gap.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about our work and bills in this picture. I do not need to invent a crisis to justify checking a file properly.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you try a small AI tool?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have never used one, and I would not put a client's contract into an unapproved system. If the partners run a supervised paid trial later, I can look at the result before deciding.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why keep so much cash?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The mortgage and children make eleven months feel like freedom to say no to a poor job offer. It is money we already have, not a new saving plan.

say: I would keep a **paper trail** and named reviewer on returns.
I would explain the **tax file** to clients myself.
think: Our **eleven-month reserve** and high wage make this mild case manageable.
Nearby accounting firms give us **real alternatives** if the current job changes.
do: Keep **paid contractor accounts** and file signed payment slips with returns.
Retain the **existing cash reserve** for a real income gap.
feel: I feel **calm** about our work and bills.
S0.quote: I do not need to invent a crisis to justify checking a file properly.
fieldNote: His **high pay** and eleven months saved support calm without implying he is eager to adopt AI.
Keeping an existing reserve is **capital retention**, not a claim that he is adding new money each month.

steps.text: Keep paid contractor returns with signed completion slips and retain existing cash reserve

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: AI could read the contracts and check the numbers I spend my day checking. Robots would reach building sites later, but our office would feel the change first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the firm to keep a named professional responsible for every AI-drafted return. I would ask the staff association to demand paid notice before any team-hours cut.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think the partners might use one senior signer for several teams, and my own paid hours could realistically fall. Eleven months saved gives us time, but I do not want Mira's wage carrying the mortgage by itself.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask my manager Celia for a one-month paid comparison of AI-drafted contractor returns against signed originals, only with her written approval and anonymised files. If she refuses, I would keep checking the paid files I am assigned; if the comparison passes, I would still require written approval before any live use. If my hours are cut in the first year, I would seek a posted senior accounts role only with written wage, hours and start date that cover the mortgage and our actual school pickup rota.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about my own paid hours, though I am not short of cash tomorrow. My qualification cannot stop a partner deciding one signer is enough.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you learn the tool yourself?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only during a paid, supervised trial; I am slow to trust a new screen. I would compare each flagged retention payment with the signed slip before I let a client see it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the association do?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask it to seek written notice and paid time for checking, not pretend it can veto every change. I would keep the current paid shifts while they are offered.

say: I would require a **named signer** for AI-drafted returns.
I would seek **paid notice** through the staff association.
think: My own **senior hours** could shrink if one signer covers several teams.
Mira's salary alone would strain our **mortgage**, despite our reserve.
do: Compare **anonymised returns** with originals for one approved paid supervised month; otherwise keep paid checks, requiring signed approval before live use.
Ask the **staff association** for paid notice and retain offered paid shifts.
After cuts take a **posted senior job** only with written mortgage-covering wage, hours, start and pickup fit.
feel: I feel **anxious** about losing paid hours.
S1.quote: My qualification cannot stop a partner deciding one signer is enough.
fieldNote: He would examine AI only through a **paid supervised comparison** and never on live files without written approval.
The association request concerns **notice and paid checks**; his job search still requires an actual posted vacancy.

steps.text: Learn on anonymised originals for one approved paid month under supervision; otherwise retain checks
Use live returns only after passing comparison and written approval
Ask staff association for paid notice while keeping offered shifts
After cuts take posted senior job with written mortgage-covering wage hours start and pickup

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: AGI in 2028 could judge the contracts and draft the entire tax return, so my desk is exposed then. Robots around 2031 would reach physical site work later, not give my accounts three extra years.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the association to press for a written severance and notice schedule. I would tell colleagues not to give away client records to an AGI system without a named accountable signer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect the firm to remove my senior accounting post as preparation fees collapse. We have eleven months of expenses saved, but losing my high wage would still force a mortgage plan; I have been waking early and counting the months.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would ask the association for severance terms and keep every paid return offered until the post actually ends. In the first year after 2028, if it ends, I would use the reserve for bills while applying to posted contract-audit supervisor roles, taking one only with written pay, hours and start date covering the mortgage and school pickup. A contract-audit desk is also thinking work, so I would treat a paid offer as a bridge.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed because I expect our main wage to go. Eleven months buys decisions, not a guarantee that a local firm will hire me.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why contract audit if AGI can read contracts?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: It is a bridge I know how to do, not a safe harbour. I will not promise my children that a different job title defeats AGI.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would Mira change her work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner Mira could take a few more school-office hours if offered, but I would not count them before the school confirms them. Our mortgage must be covered by the written wage on any job I take.

say: I would demand **written severance** and notice through the association.
I would insist on a **named signer** for client records.
think: I expect my **senior post** to go when preparation fees collapse.
Our **eleven-month reserve** buys time but cannot replace my high wage indefinitely.
do: Ask the **association** for severance and keep offered paid returns until dismissal.
After loss, use the **reserve for bills** during the posted contract-audit search.
Take a **posted supervisor job** only with written mortgage-covering pay, hours, start and pickup.
feel: I feel **alarmed** by expected loss of my main wage.
S2.quote: Eleven months buys decisions, not a guarantee that a local firm will hire me.
fieldNote: He expects **2028 desk displacement** even though capable robots arrive around 2031.
The contract-audit post is explicitly a **paid bridge** with written terms; his existing savings fund bills during any gap.

steps.text: Ask association for severance and keep offered paid returns until dismissal
After loss use reserve for bills; take posted job with written mortgage-covering pay hours start pickup

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years lets me show which clients still pay for a person to explain a retention-payment dispute. AGI reaches the accounting desk in 2031; robots in 2034 are a separate later change for sites.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the partners to price a human dispute review and assign the hours, rather than call unpaid calls a career path. I would tell the team the job needs a budget line.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The routine return fee may fall, but a funded client-resolution role could use my experience. We have enough savings to test demand without raiding the children's school money, provided I keep earning while work is available.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would take one paid contractor dispute meeting each quarter only if Celia assigns it within my paid hours and the firm bills the client. I would keep preparing paid returns; before or after 2031, I would take a posted client-resolution role only with written pay, hours and start date covering the mortgage and pickup. If return work ends first in the year after 2031, I would use the reserve for bills while seeking that qualifying offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about my own fee income, but five years lets me test a real paid service. I will not turn a corridor chat into a forecast salary.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you take a course for that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I already have the chartered qualification and years of dispute work. I would consider additional study only if a firm pays the fee and paid time for a defined post.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if clients do not pay for the meeting?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would stop offering the extra meeting and keep the paid returns still assigned. A friendly builder is not a billed client role.

say: I would seek a **priced dispute review** on paid hours.
I would ask for a **budgeted role**, not unpaid calls.
think: Routine **return fees** could fall after 2031 AGI.
A **funded client role** might use my experience if clients actually pay.
do: Lead **quarterly billed disputes** only if Celia assigns them on paid time; stop if clients refuse the fee.
Keep **paid returns** while available; after loss, use the reserve for bills during the search.
Take a **posted client-resolution job** before or after 2031 only with written mortgage-covering pay, hours, start and pickup.
feel: I feel **anxious** about the future fee income.
S3.quote: I will not turn a corridor chat into a forecast salary.
fieldNote: His measure of demand is **one billed meeting** assigned quarterly, not client goodwill.
The strong reserve supports a search after loss, while a job move remains conditional on **posted written terms**.

steps.text: Keep paid returns and lead quarterly disputes only when assigned on paid billed time
After loss use reserve; take posted client job with written mortgage-covering pay hours start pickup

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten years means the children will be older and the mortgage smaller before AGI reaches our tax desk in 2036. Robots in 2039 do not delay the thinking-work change for accounts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the partners for dated staffing plans and a real paid dispute role. I would tell colleagues a title without a wage line is only stationery.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I still expect return preparation to be cheaper, but our high wage and eleven months saved mean we can pay down the loan rather than rush into a new occupation. I will not claim the future office will still need my exact post.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would pay an extra one hundred from my monthly salary toward mortgage principal only if the lender confirms it is penalty-free and regular bills are covered; if the lender charges a penalty, I would deposit that amount as cash only after regular bills are covered. I would keep paid contractor returns while offered and take a posted dispute lead role before or after 2036 only with written pay, hours and start date covering the remaining mortgage and workable family travel. In the first year after 2036, if returns end first, I would use the reserve for bills during the search.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about a distant change in my post, but the decade gives us room to reduce debt. That is a plan with a monthly number, not an exit speech.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you retire early?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, at 43 with children and a mortgage I still want paid work. Savings are a bridge, not a pension.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who decides family travel works?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner Mira and I would compare the posted hours with the children's school route before I sign. I will not accept a start date and invent a pickup later.

say: I would demand **dated staffing plans** and a paid dispute role.
I would say an unpaid title is **only stationery**.
think: Our high wage and reserve allow **measured mortgage repayment** before the desk changes.
do: Pay **one hundred extra monthly** toward principal only if penalty-free after bills; otherwise deposit cash.
Keep **paid contractor returns** while offered; after loss, use reserve for bills during search.
Take a **posted dispute lead role** only with written mortgage-covering pay, hours, start and family-travel fit.
feel: I feel **uneasy** about the distant post change.
S4.quote: Savings are a bridge, not a pension.
fieldNote: His long horizon and **high current wage** support new principal payments without treating retained savings as new deposits.
Every job move needs **posted written terms** and a workable school route checked with Mira.

steps.text: Pay one hundred extra monthly if penalty-free after bills; otherwise deposit cash
Keep paid returns while offered; after loss use reserve for bills
Take posted dispute job with written mortgage-covering pay hours start and family travel

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because it could remove my high wage before I have time to prove a different paid service. Written notice, fair severance and an actual posted role with mortgage-covering pay would help, even with eleven months saved.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask who has to explain a wrong AGI return to the builder. The client cannot appeal to a blank signature line.

headlineQuote: The client cannot appeal to a blank signature line.
portrait: Adam is a **43-year-old senior accountant** with a master's and chartered qualification who leads contractor accounts.
His **high wage**, eleven-month reserve and many local firms give him choices despite a mortgage and two children.
He **never uses AI** and requires a written, paid historical trial before considering it.
He asks for **association notice** and tests billed dispute work before changing roles.
biggestWorry: The **2028 AGI** picture could erase his high wage before he proves another paid service.
whatWouldHelp: He wants **written notice and severance**, plus a posted role with mortgage-covering terms.
